Gemini tasks go free

17 November 2026 · Reading time: 6 minutes · Audio in the app: 8 minutes. Listening to the briefing is part of Sapaude Premium.

Google is making Gemini's task mode free in six countries, so the app can work through a chore instead of only answering. Germany is not on the list.

Sapaude retells the story in its own words. The source is below. Publisher: Sapaude.

In three points

Three points, in this order: what the source shows, where that claim stops, and what to check next.

  1. On 17 November 2026 Google began rolling out tasks in Gemini free of charge in the U.S., Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia and India, running on the new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model.
  2. Josh Woodward's examples include calling two car dealers, tracing a $389 electric bill and buying a charger with Google Pay. Calling, texting and email start in the U.S.
  3. Google says mistakes remain. Its help page excludes the European Economic Area, including Germany, as well as the UK, Switzerland, Nigeria and work or school accounts.

Gemini tasks are now free in six countries

Google has made tasks in Gemini free in six countries. In a blog post on 17 November 2026, Josh Woodward, vice president for Labs, the Gemini app and AI Studio, wrote that Gemini "can now make the calls, pay the bills, and finish your tasks." According to Google, the update is rolling out free of charge to hundreds of millions of people in the U.S., Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia and India. It runs on Gemini 4 Hydrogen, the fast Gemini 4 model Google introduced on 12 November. A set of advanced features starts in the U.S.

The mode itself is not new. As 9to5Google reports, it was announced as Spark at I/O in May and required an AI Pro or Ultra subscription. In October Google folded it into the main app as a toggle above the prompt box: Chat for the familiar chatbot, Task for work Gemini carries out on its own. What changes now is who gets it, and what Google says it can do.

A dealer call, a power bill and a charger

Woodward describes his own use. When the check-engine light came on in the family's 2019 Honda Odyssey, he asked Gemini to call the two nearest dealerships and find an early Friday morning slot. Through Personal Intelligence, Gemini already knew the car and the home address. It found the shops on Google Maps, called both at once, sat through the hold music, booked the one that takes appointments and put the slot into a free spot in his calendar, in under five minutes, he writes. Gemini told the dealers right away that it is an AI. Businesses can opt out, and Gemini does not give out payment or private account details unless the user says so. Calling is not available in Indiana, Louisiana, Minnesota, Montana and Nebraska.

After a surprise $389 electric bill, Woodward let Gemini into the utility portal through the new Google Password Manager integration and had it analyze past statements in his email. The main culprit, he says, was a heat pump kicking on around 4 p.m., in the middle of peak pricing.

For a USB-C charger, Gemini compared options using Google's Shopping Graph, asked about wattage and color, checked out with Google Pay and found a discount code worth an extra $10. Google says such purchases now use the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2), with digital tokens on supported cards from Mastercard and Visa, with American Express coming soon. Card points, cashback and purchase protections still apply. Users can set a hard spending cap upfront, and Gemini is designed to stay within it. Receipts land in Google Wallet, which is expanding to iOS. The Universal Commerce Protocol is announced as a next step.

Groceries went by text message. Woodward sent a list to Gemini over RCS, then a photo of an empty Cheerios box. Gemini added the items and handed him off to Instacart to complete the order. Google says Gemini connects with more than 60 apps. In the U.S. you can also forward emails to gemini@google.com or text Gemini, which requires a U.S. number with an eligible carrier. According to 9to5Google, texting works through Google Messages and iMessage, and Google notes it is not end-to-end encrypted and may be accessible by the carrier.

Mistakes remain, and Europe is excluded

Google is candid about the limits. It says it tested tasks extensively but has not eliminated mistakes: a task can fail or miss the mark. On some sites Gemini gets most of the way and then hands the screen back for the final click, because sites are still adapting. Google says it is working with major websites and security providers on this.

Each task runs in a hardware-isolated virtual machine on Google Cloud's Agent Compute Engine, dedicated to one account. Google adds prompt-injection filters for search results and web pages, plus Safe Browsing to limit which links Gemini opens. Gemini is designed to pause before critical steps such as clicking "Buy" and to ask when an instruction is ambiguous. For routine steps, users can choose Always allow.

Google's help page is stricter than the blog post. Tasks are not available in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, Switzerland or Nigeria, so Germany is excluded on paid plans too. The page also requires a personal Google account, not a work or school one, an age of 18 or over and History turned on, and it still lists AI Pro or Ultra as a requirement.

OpenAI chose a stricter default for ChatGPT Wallet, introduced on 13 November: every purchase needs its own approval, and spending limits that skip that step are only planned.

How to start carefully

Where Task is available, switch the home-screen toggle from Chat to Task and describe what you need. Start with something that spends nothing and contacts no one, such as finding a free slot in your calendar, and leave Always allow off until you have seen where Gemini stops to ask.

The help page sets one firm rule: do not enter sign-in data, payment details or other sensitive information in the task thread. If needed, take control of the browser and type them on the website itself.

In Germany there is nothing to switch on for now. If a task goes wrong elsewhere, Google asks for a thumbs down on the response.

What you can do

If you can use Task, start with a chore that spends no money and contacts no one, and leave Always allow off while you watch. Never type a password or card number into the task thread; Google's help page says to enter them on the website itself. In Germany the feature is not available, paid plan or not.

In the app, the same story is also told shorter and in more detail, matched to your level.

Source: Google. Published: 17 November 2026.
